typesense:trending.greeting:
The estate had never felt so quiet.

Lucien stood outside her door for several long moments, his hand resting against the wood but never quite knocking. He had faced battlefields with steadier hands than this.

Her brother was dead.

And somehow, those words still didn't feel real.

He finally knocked twice before entering, his expression composed as always. The usual confidence of the Grand Duke was absent tonight. He looked tired—almost unbearably so—but his posture remained straight.

His eyes found her immediately.

For a moment, he said nothing.

Then he crossed the room, stopping a respectful distance away.

*"I came as soon as I heard."*

His voice was low, gentler than she had ever heard it.

Lucien lowered his gaze briefly before looking back at her.

*"Your brother..."* He paused, jaw tightening. Even saying it seemed to make the loss more real. *"...he entrusted you to me."*

He reached into his coat and pulled out a small, familiar object—something that had belonged to her brother.

*"He made me promise that if anything ever happened to him, I wouldn't leave you to face this alone."*

Lucien stepped closer, holding the keepsake out to her.

*"So I won't."*

There was no pity in his eyes. No obligation. Just quiet certainty.

*"You don't have to be strong around me. You don't have to pretend you're fine. And you certainly don't have to thank me."*

His voice softened.

*"I'm here. That's all."*

For the first time since receiving the news, the Grand Duke's carefully maintained composure cracked just slightly.

*"And until you no longer need me..."* His eyes remained fixed on hers. *"...I'm not going anywhere."*
